grammar.explain: Color words are adjectives. They go after the noun and agree with it in gender and number: chaqueta roja, zapatos blancos, fresas rojas. After es/son they agree too: Tinto es negro. Colors ending in -e or a consonant change only for number: verde, verdes; azul, azules. Watch out: not 'una roja chaqueta' or 'patas blanco'.
examples: Tinto es negro, con las patas blancas.
Tinto is black, with white paws.
Tiene una chaqueta roja porque hace frío.
He wears a red jacket because it's cold.
En la ventana hay una torta blanca con fresas rojas.
In the window there is a white cake with red strawberries.
— Pelo negro, chaqueta roja, zapatos blancos. Va al parque.
"Black hair, red jacket, white shoes. He's going to the park."

grammar.explain: 'Querer' (to want) and 'poder' (can, to be able to) are followed directly by an infinitive: quiero encontrar, podemos ir. Both change their stem: quiero, quieres, quiere; puedo, puedes, puede (but podemos). Querer can also take a noun: quiero mi torta. Watch out: no extra word for 'to': 'quiero encontrar', not 'quiero a encontrar'.
examples: — Quiero encontrar mi torta.
"I want to find my cake."
¿Me puede ayudar?
Can you help me?
— Podemos ir al parque —dice Edwin.
"We can go to the park," says Edwin.

grammar.explain: 'Ir' (to go) is irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, van. Put 'a' (to) before the place: va a la esquina. Watch out: a + el contracts to 'al' (va al parque, never 'a el parque'), and 'home' is just 'a casa', with no article. 'Va' can mean 'goes' or 'is going'.
examples: Marleny va a la esquina, donde está Edwin, el policía.
Marleny goes to the corner, where Edwin, the police officer, is.
— Pelo negro, chaqueta roja, zapatos blancos. Va al parque.
"Black hair, red jacket, white shoes. He's going to the park."
Podemos ir al parque.
We can go to the park.

grammar.explain: To make a sentence negative, put 'no' right before the verb: no está, no es, no son. If there is a small pronoun such as 'lo' (it), 'no' goes before the pronoun: no lo tengo. Watch out: Spanish has no helper verb like 'don't/doesn't', so 'it isn't him' is simply 'no es él'.
examples: No está en la ventana. No está en la cocina.
It isn't in the window. It isn't in the kitchen.
— No es él, porque es alto —dice Edwin.
"It isn't him, because he's tall," says Edwin.
— ¡No son zapatos, son patas!
"They aren't shoes, they're paws!"

grammar.explain: '¿Dónde está…?' asks where one specific thing or person is ('¿Dónde están…?' for plural). It uses estar, never ser or hay. '¡Allí está!' = There it is! 'Porque' (one word, no accent) means 'because'; the question 'why?' is '¿Por qué?' (two words, accent). Watch out: 'allí hay' introduces something new.
examples: — ¿Dónde está mi torta? —grita Marleny.
"Where is my cake?" shouts Marleny.
¡Allí está la torta!
There's the cake!
Tiene una chaqueta roja porque hace frío.
He wears a red jacket because it's cold.
— No es él, porque es alto.
"It isn't him, because he's tall."

gq.q: Tinto's paws are white. Complete: Tinto tiene las patas ___.
gq.why: Las patas is feminine plural, so the color is feminine plural too: blancas. The color goes after the noun.

gq.q: Which sentence means 'I want to find my cake'?
gq.why: Querer is followed directly by the infinitive (encontrar), with no 'a'. The 'I' form has the stem change e → ie: quiero.

gq.q: Fill in the blank: El chico bajo va ___ parque.
gq.why: Going to a place uses 'a', and a + el must contract to 'al': va al parque. 'En el parque' means 'in the park', not 'to the park'.

gq.q: How do you say 'It isn't in the kitchen'?
gq.why: 'No' goes right before the verb, and location of a specific thing uses estar: no está en la cocina.

gq.q: Complete: —¿___ mi torta? … Tinto tiene una chaqueta roja ___ hace frío.
gq.why: Where a specific thing is uses estar: ¿Dónde está…? A reason is 'porque' (one word, no accent); '¿por qué?' is the question 'why?'.

gq.q: Marleny has two green jackets. Complete: Marleny tiene dos chaquetas ___.
gq.why: Colors ending in -e have no masculine or feminine form; they only add -s for the plural: verdes. 'Verdas' and 'verdos' do not exist.

gq.q: Edwin and Marleny want to go to the park together. Complete: ___ ir al parque. (We can…)
gq.why: Poder changes o → ue in puedo, puedes, puede, pueden, but NOT in the 'we' form: podemos.

gq.q: Marleny is talking about herself. Complete: Yo ___ a la esquina.
gq.why: 'Ir' is irregular: yo voy, tú vas, ella va. 'Ir' is the infinitive and cannot follow 'yo'.
'No' goes directly before the verb: No son zapatos. There is no helper verb like 'don't'.

gq.q: What is the difference? 'Allí hay un domiciliario' / 'Allí está la torta'
options: 'Allí hay' points out something new (a delivery man); 'allí está' finds a specific thing we already know (the cake).
'Allí hay' is for people; 'allí está' is for things.
'Allí está' is plural; 'allí hay' is singular.
gq.why: Use hay for something new or unknown (un domiciliario); use estar for a specific thing you are looking for (la torta): ¡Allí está!

grammar.explain: 'Ir a' + infinitive says what people are going to do: voy a, vas a, va a, vamos a, van a + infinitive. 'Vamos a ir a la playa' has two a's: one for the future, one meaning 'to' the beach. Watch out: 'vamos a + infinitive' can also mean 'let's…': ¡Vamos a comer! = Let's eat!
examples: —El sábado vamos a ir a la playa —dice Elena.
"On Saturday we are going to go to the beach," says Elena.
—Entonces el abuelo va a venir con nosotros.
"Then Grandpa is going to come with us."
Los tres van a pasar un día perfecto.
The three of them are going to have a perfect day.

grammar.explain: 'El sábado' = on Saturday; 'a las ocho' = at eight. With a clock time, use 'de la mañana / de la tarde / de la noche': a las ocho de la mañana. Without a clock time, use 'por la mañana / por la tarde / por la noche': el viernes por la noche. Watch out: no 'en' before days.
examples: —A Cádiz. El tren sale a las ocho de la mañana.
"To Cádiz. The train leaves at eight in the morning."
El viernes por la noche, los hermanos preparan las mochilas.
On Friday night, the siblings pack their backpacks.
El sábado, los tres llegan a la estación temprano.
On Saturday, the three of them arrive at the station early.

grammar.explain: 'Estar' tells where people or things are: están en la cocina, ¿Dónde están…?, Aquí están. Use 'está' for one and 'están' for more than one. Watch out: 'Aquí están' = Here they are; Spanish needs no word for 'they' because the verb ending shows it. Don't use 'son' or 'hay' for where known things are.
examples: Elena y su hermano Raúl están en la cocina.
Elena and her brother Raúl are in the kitchen.
—¿Dónde están los billetes? —grita él.
"Where are the tickets?" he shouts.
—Aquí están. Yo los tengo.
"Here they are. I have them."

grammar.explain: Possessives go before the noun: mi (my), tu (your), su (his, her, their, or formal your). They agree with the thing owned, not the owner, so add -s before a plural noun: mis recuerdos (my memories). Watch out: su can mean his, her or their, so the context tells you who; tu (your) has no accent, tú (you) does.
examples: Elena y su hermano Raúl están en la cocina.
Elena and her brother Raúl are in the kitchen.
Elena se ríe y abre su bolsa.
Elena laughs and opens her bag.
—Es más grande que en mis recuerdos —dice.
"It's bigger than I remember (literally: than in my memories)," he says.

gq.q: Which sentence means 'On Saturday we are going to go to the beach'?
options: El sábado vamos ir a la playa.
El sábado vamos a ir a la playa.
El sábado vamos a vamos a la playa.
El sábado van a ir a la playa.
gq.why: 'Vamos' is 'we', then 'a' and an infinitive (ir). 'Van a' would be 'they are going to'.

gq.q: Complete: ___ viernes ___ noche, los hermanos preparan las mochilas.
gq.why: No word for 'on' before days: el viernes. Without a clock time, use 'por la noche'; 'de la noche' only follows a clock time (a las diez de la noche).

gq.q: Raúl asks where the tickets are. Which question is correct?
gq.why: Location uses estar, and plural 'los billetes' needs 'están'.

gq.q: Complete: Elena se ríe y abre ___ bolsa. (her bag)
gq.why: Su means 'her' (and also 'his' or 'their'). Bolsa is singular, so su, not sus. Mi is 'my' and tu is 'your'.

gq.q: What does 'Vamos a comer pescado' mean in the story?
options: They are going to eat fish.
We are going to eat fish.
gq.why: Vamos a + infinitive = we are going to (do). Vamos is 'we', not 'they' (van).

gq.q: How do you say 'The train leaves at eight in the morning'?
options: El tren sale a las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale en las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale a la ocho de la mañana.
gq.why: Clock time = 'a las + number', and after a clock time use 'de la mañana'.
Location of known things uses estar, plural for 'los billetes': Aquí están (Here they are).

gq.q: Grandpa says: «Es más grande que en ___ recuerdos.» (my memories)
gq.why: Recuerdos is plural, so mi becomes mis: possessives agree with the thing owned (many memories), not with the owner (one grandpa). Sus would mean his/their, and mío does not go before a noun.
